name: Abū Fayd Muʾarrij ibn ʿAmr al-Sadūsī
summary: Basran master of the lexicon and of Arabic, a senior pupil of al-Khalīl and of Abū Zayd, who said he came from the desert knowing nothing of analogy and learned it in al-Khalīl's circle.
bio: Muʾarrij learned from Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī and was one of al-Khalīl's senior students; he heard ḥadīth from Shuʿba ibn al-Ḥajjāj and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, and the Yazīdīs learned from him. By his own account he came from the desert knowing nothing of analogy (qiyās) and first learned it in al-Khalīl's circle.
Al-Zubaydī lists him both with the grammarians of Basra (sixth generation) and with its lexicographers. He went to Khurasan with the caliph al-Maʾmūn.
uncertain: Ibn al-Anbārī gives no year of death; 195/810 is the date in TDV.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 179–184
